explanation: A hyperbola has two mirror branches that open left and right, hugging a pair of straight asymptotes with slope ±b/a. The vertices sit at (±a, 0) where the branches turn around, and the foci sit farther out at (±c, 0) with c = sqrt(a² + b²). Increase a to push the vertices apart; increase b to steepen the asymptotes and flare the branches open.
bullets: Vertices are at (±a, 0); the branches open along the x-axis.
The branches approach the asymptotes y = ±(b/a)x but never touch them.
Foci are at (±c, 0) with c² = a² + b² (note the PLUS, unlike an ellipse).
